location: sections/limits.tex:21-22 (bullet), limits.tex:362 (title); also abstract.tex:22-23, intro.tex:196-197, conclusion.tex:16-18, growth.tex:282-284
issue: The summary 'under rETH the exponent of kappa cannot be o(p)' omits the qualifier that the polynomial in I has fixed degree. Prop prop:lbproduct only excludes running times f(p)(kappa I)^{p/psi(p)}, in particular f(p)kappa^{a(p)}I^C with C constant.
evidence: On the hard instances both kappa and I are poly(kN_0) (App. G.2, 'Conditioning'), so the reduction cannot separate the exponent of kappa from the degree in I. An algorithm with running time kappa^3 I^p has kappa-exponent 3 = o(p) but is not of the excluded form. It contradicts neither Prop 10.6 nor ETH: it gives N_0^{O(k)} on the clique instances and 2^{O(I)} on the instances of Prop 10.1, where log kappa = O(I). Theorem 1.2(c) and the sentence after Prop 10.6 ('in the sense a(p) <= p/psi(p) above') are precise; the shorthand summaries are not.
fix: limits.tex 21-22: 'under randomized ETH the exponent of $\kappa$ in a bound $f(p)\kappa^{a(p)}I^{O(1)}$ cannot be $o(p)$, already for integer box quadratics (Proposition~\ref{prop:lbproduct})'. Add the same qualifier ('in a bound f(p)kappa^{a(p)}poly(I)') in the abstract, intro 196-197, conclusion 16-18 and Remark rem:fpt (growth.tex 282-284).

issue: The comparison between CT and the value-oracle barrier is imprecise. limits.tex says no algorithm 'can do the same' under unknown set growth. The intro says such an algorithm 'needs a number of queries that grows with the accuracy', but this is also true of CT under point growth.
evidence: Under point growth CT makes about 2(J+1)K^p evaluations with J = O(I+q) stages (Thm thm:approx), so its query count also grows with the accuracy, logarithmically in 1/eps. The real separation is the rate. Prop prop:oraclebarrier gives at least (1/(2 sqrt(6 eps)) - 1)^n - 1 = Omega(eps^{-n/2}) queries on f = 0 with kappa_S = 1, against O(log(1/eps)) for CT.
fix: limits.tex 609-613: 'Under point growth, CT uses a number of nodes per coordinate that does not depend on the accuracy, and hence f(p,kappa) O(I+q) evaluations. Proposition~\ref{prop:oraclebarrier} shows that under growth towards an unknown set every algorithm in this information model, even with exact derivatives, needs $\Omega(\varepsilon^{-n/2})$ queries, already for $n=p=1$ on an instance with $\kappa_S=1$.' intro.tex 207-208: replace 'needs a number of queries that grows with the accuracy' with 'needs a number of queries polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$ (at least of order $\varepsilon^{-n/2}$)'.

issue: Remark lim:rem:dk says kappa (and, in limits.tex, nu/g) is 'exponential in the input length'. Under the paper's encoding the input length is Theta(k log k), so the bound is 2^{Theta(I/log I)}, not 2^{Omega(I)}.
evidence: For c = 2^k the DK instance has N = 5k+7 variables and O(k) monomials with bounded coefficients. The input length I counts binary variable indices and the decomposition (Section 3, 'Encoding'), so I = Theta(k log k). Then kappa >= 80(k+1)4^k = 2^{Theta(k)} = 2^{Theta(I/log I)}, and nu/g >= 4c = 2^{k+2}. These bounds are superpolynomial but not 2^{Omega(I)}. Elsewhere the paper uses exact forms such as 2^{O(I)} and 2^{I^delta}.
fix: appendix-lbproduct.tex 31-33: 'For $c=2^k$ there are $N=5k+7$ variables and coefficients bounded by five, so $\kappa\ge80(k+1)4^k$ is exponential in the number of variables (and $2^{\Omega(I/\log I)}$ in the input length), consistent with Corollary~\ref{lim:cor:nopolylog}.' limits.tex 204: replace 'exponential in the input length' with 'exponential in the number of variables'.

issue: The running-sum encoding is credited to Bienstock-Muñoz (2018) without a locator. That paper is about LP formulations, and the encoding appears only in its appendix.
